title: ₹500 Ka Blood Test: Lab Owner Ke Paas Asli Mein Kitna Bachta Hai?
description: Reasoning: our medical store and ICU bed reels show healthcare economics is of high interest. A diagnostic lab is the next dream-to-own business in that vein (many pharma and science graduates consider it), and franchise terms are public, so the numbers can be researched.
text:
# HISAAB FACT SHEET: Diagnostic collection centre / lab franchise (India)

Reel angle: a ₹500 blood test, what it costs the lab, who gets what, and the break-even patients per day.

**Read this first**
- No listed chain publishes its franchisee revenue share. Brands don't publish the share. [https://www.clinikpe.com/pathology-collection-centre-franchise-cost-profit-margin-and-how-to-start/]
- Franchise-portal figures conflict with each other and are often old. I flag this wherever it matters.
- Items marked DERIVED are my arithmetic on sourced numbers, not figures a company stated. Check them before they go in the script.

---

## 1. The hook: price vs real cost

**What the patient pays**
- CBC prices on labs' own pages on 26 Sep 2026: ₹250 (Dr Lal PathLabs, Mumbai) to ₹449 (Apollo 24|7 base price), with Redcliffe ₹299, Tata 1mg ₹329, Metropolis ₹340 and Healthians ₹353. [https://ayuapp.com/blog/cbc-blood-test-cost-india]
- The same source lists the official CGHS rate for a CBC at ₹300. CBC test price in India today: ₹250 at Dr Lal, ₹340 Metropolis, ₹449 Apollo 24|7 vs the official CGHS rate of ₹300. [https://ayuapp.com/blog/cbc-blood-test-cost-india]
- Dr Lal's Bengaluru home-collection CBC is ₹340. It is a 20-parameter panel. [https://www.lalpathlabs.com/test/pathology/complete-blood-count/bengaluru]

**What the machine and reagent cost per test (hard to source; use with care)**
- A diagnostics-equipment guide puts reagent cost at ₹5-15 per test depending on equipment and reagent efficiency. It is a vendor and marketplace guide, not an audited figure. [https://www.clinikpe.com/lab-equipment-price/]
- Its 5-year ownership example: Equipment Purchase ₹10,00,000, AMC (5 years @ 10%) ₹5,00,000, Reagents & Consumables ₹12,00,000. [https://www.clinikpe.com/lab-equipment-price/]
- A practising pathologist's costing slides (Dr Kunal Sehgal, MD) say cost of reagent and controls is negligible for most tests. [https://sehgalpathlab.com/assets/frontend/pdf/presentations/CBC/Costing-of-Common-Laboratory-tests.pdf]
- The same slides cost a CBC in a small lab like this:
  - Fixed cost ₹100.
  - Sample collection ₹10.
  - Report printing ₹2.
  - Pathologist review ₹25, which is ₹1250 per day for 50 cases.
  - The analyser costs ₹4.5 lakh every 5 years.
  - [https://sehgalpathlab.com/assets/frontend/pdf/presentations/CBC/Costing-of-Common-Laboratory-tests.pdf]
  - The slide is a small-lab example, undated and partly garbled in the extract. Use it for the idea that the fixed cost per patient is much bigger than the reagent cost, not as an exact cost per test.
- Analyser prices:
  - Basic equipment such as centrifuges and microscopes can cost between ₹10,000 and ₹2 lakh, while advanced analyzers such as CBC machines and biochemistry analyzers can range from ₹3 lakh to ₹25 lakh or more. [https://www.clinikpe.com/lab-equipment-price/]
  - A 3-part or 5-part haematology analyser is listed at ₹2.5L–₹25L. [https://www.clinikpe.com/pathology-lab-setup-guide/]

**What a listed chain actually spends per ₹ of revenue (Dr Lal PathLabs, FY26)**
- Revenue from operations was ₹27,629 million (₹2,763 crore). [https://media.lalpathlabs.com/2026-06/8deca5c7-9650-4aa0-81d8-70c090ca0262.pdf]
- Expense lines, in ₹ million: Material Costs 5,346; Employee Benefits 5,033; Collection Centre Fees 4,024. [https://www.bullscreen.in/news/dr-lal-pathlabs-limited-announces-fy26-q4-results-declares-dividend-approves-mumbai-acquisition-and-dubai-expansion/]
- The cost of materials consumed remained steady at 19.2% of revenue in Q4 FY26. [https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/dr-lal-pathlabs-q1-results-cmryqg8ny9gxt0zl44xezenwi]
- DERIVED: collection centre fees ÷ revenue = about 14.6%. Employee cost ÷ revenue = about 18.2%. So of every ₹100 Dr Lal bills, about ₹19 goes to reagents and consumables and about ₹15 to collection-centre partners. Collection-centre fees are not only franchisee commission, so treat 14.6% as a ceiling for "the franchise share of total revenue".
- Profit left: FY26 PBT of ₹669 crore, a margin of 24.2%. [https://finance.yahoo.com/sectors/healthcare/articles/dr-lal-pathlabs-ltd-bom-190114978.html]
- Net profit: FY26 net profit was Rs 510 crore (up 3.6% YoY), and EBITDA was Rs 752 crore with a 27.2% margin. [https://www.multibagg.ai/market-pulse/articles/dr-lal-pathlabs-q4-fy26-results-cmoqvjpk579u5p50js5q4qvqq]
- Metropolis: FY26 revenue ₹1,646 crore, EBITDA ₹401 crore, EBITDA margin 24.4%, PAT ₹191 crore. [https://scanx.trade/stock-market-news/companies/metropolis-healthcare-fy26-results-revenue-up-24-pat-rises-31/46756400]

---

## 2. Why packages and home collection matter

**Nobody gets just one test**
- Dr Lal's revenue per patient was INR956 in Q4 FY26, up 7.8% from INR887 in Q4 FY25.
